profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting at a rural health system between the nurse-led chronic disease care coordination program and the population health analytics team. They are preparing a steering committee update on patients with poorly controlled diabetes, hypertension, and CHF enrolled in the integrated care program, including outcome trends, education completion, and utilization changes. The agenda is to align on the patient roster, confirm what will go into the monthly outcomes table, reconcile referral and education handoffs, and make sure both teams are using the same supporting materials for the presentation. The expected outcome is an apparently agreed plan for which patients and measures will appear in the update and who will provide the final supporting data artifacts.

members.name: Laura Benton
members.expertise: Chronic disease care management, rural telehealth follow-up, care transition workflows
members.background: Laura oversees certified care coordination nurses serving several rural clinics and is responsible for enrollment follow-up, phone outreach, education reinforcement, and specialty referral tracking for high-risk diabetes, hypertension, and CHF patients.
members.private_state: She wants the program's work to be represented fairly in the steering update, especially for patients who are still enrolled but difficult to reach, and she is worried that operational realities in rural care are often flattened by registry rules.
hidden_assumptions: A patient remains active in the program until the nurse team formally discharges them, even if they have not had a documented touch recently.
Baseline clinical values should reflect the point just before active nurse management begins, not the earlier referral trigger that first identified the patient.
DSME completion includes telehealth education series and one-on-one sessions delivered by the program's certified nurses when they cover the same content.
Recent hospital use can appropriately include patient-reported outside admissions while records are still being obtained, because care coordination acts on that information immediately.

members.name: Evan Morales
members.expertise: Clinical registry reporting, quality dashboards, EHR measure logic, utilization data integration
members.background: Evan maintains the chronic disease registry and prepares monthly reporting extracts for leadership using EHR documentation, education module flags, ADT feeds, and prebuilt denominator logic across the rural network.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the steering committee packet methodologically consistent with prior reports and avoid introducing manually interpreted definitions that cannot be reproduced next month.
hidden_assumptions: Active patients are those currently flagged by registry logic, which requires recent documented coordinator activity rather than just open enrollment status.
Baseline should be the first qualifying abnormal measure that triggered inclusion, because that is the stable anchor for longitudinal reporting.
DSME completion only counts when the standardized accredited course is marked complete in the EHR education module.
Hospital utilization for the report should come from the ADT-based utilization feed and confirmed coded encounters, not provisional patient-reported events.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the active roster
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to the 'active patient list' for this month's steering update.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means everyone still enrolled in care coordination and not formally discharged by the nurse team, including patients currently hard to reach.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means patients marked active by the registry, which requires a recent documented coordinator touch within the system's activity window.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams routinely use the term 'active' in operations, and each has a legitimate system-based label for it, so the phrase sounds fully settled rather than in need of clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: Which value is the baseline measure
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use the patient's 'baseline A1C and BP' in the outcomes table.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the last measurement before the first nurse intake or care-plan start, because that best reflects the point just before coordinated intervention begins.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the original qualifying abnormal value that first placed the patient on the registry or referral list, even if it occurred weeks before intake.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are referring to a single-seeming event called 'baseline,' but in this workflow there are two plausible earlier measurements, and neither expects the other to mean a different one.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss patients who have 'completed DSME' and expect that figure to go into the report.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 counts completion when a patient finishes the local telehealth or one-on-one nurse-led diabetes self-management education sequence delivered by certified staff.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 counts completion only when the accredited DSME program is formally completed and coded in the EHR education module.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The label 'DSME completion' sounds like a standardized concept, and both assume the other is using the obvious institutional meaning without realizing one is thinking clinically equivalent delivery while the other is thinking reportable documentation status.

misalignment_points.topic: Which hospital admissions are included in recent utilization
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on adding the 'last six months of hospital admissions' to the patient summaries.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes local admissions plus patient-reported stays at outside rural hospitals that the nurse team is already managing around, even if records are pending.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes only admissions present in the health system's ADT/utilization feed and confirmed encounter data.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as discussing the same obvious utilization history, but one assumes a clinical care-management scope while the other assumes a reportable data-system scope.

turns.inner_thought: I need this steering packet to reflect the real state of the care coordination program, not just what happens to be easy to pull from the registry. Our nurses are still actively managing a number of rural patients who are difficult to reach, and leadership tends to forget that open enrollment and attempted follow-up are still work even when there hasn't been a recent documented touch. If we don't line up now, the program will look smaller and cleaner than it actually is.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. Before we send anything up to steering, I want to make sure the packet really reflects where the rural chronic disease cohort stands this month and that your team and mine are working off the same roster.

turns.inner_thought: Good, this should be straightforward. I refreshed the active patient list from the registry this morning, using the same logic as prior months so the committee sees a consistent trend line. I also have the usual outcome pull, education fields, and utilization columns ready. As long as we stay with standard definitions, I can reproduce all of it next month without hand-curated exceptions.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. I have the refreshed active patient list ready, along with the latest outcomes pull, plus the education and utilization fields for the monthly update.

turns.inner_thought: From the nurse team's perspective we still have 42 active patients. A few haven't answered lately, but they're still enrolled and nobody has formally discharged them. I want that understood without getting bogged down in a long operational explanation about rural phone access and patchy contact patterns.
turns.utterance: Okay, that helps. On our side, the nurses still have 42 active patients this month, and a few of those are people who are hard to reach right now but haven't come off the program.

turns.inner_thought: Her count may be higher because some recent outreach hasn't landed in the system yet, or because operations is using a broader notion of active than the registry does. I don't want to reopen definitions in this meeting; better to ask her to flag edge cases so I can see whether documentation is lagging. I'll still anchor the report to the active roster in the registry.
turns.utterance: Got it. I can work from the active roster in the registry, and if there are any names where outreach happened but the activity hasn't shown up yet, send those over and I can double-check the timing.

turns.inner_thought: Next, I need baseline A1C and BP to reflect the point just before our nurses actually began managing the patient. Some referrals sit for a few weeks before intake, and using the earlier trigger value can make the program look like it inherited a worse starting point than what was present when care coordination started. If he hears 'baseline' the same way I do, this should be easy.
turns.utterance: One thing I especially want to make sure lines up is the baseline A1C and BP in the outcomes table, since some referred patients had a gap before intake and I want that baseline tied to when nurse management really got going.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, baseline should be stable and reproducible, which is why I use the first qualifying abnormal A1C or blood pressure that got them into the registry feed in the first place. That's the cleanest anchor for longitudinal reporting. Sounds like we're aligned on keeping baseline A1C and BP in the table.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. My baseline fields already pull from the original qualifying A1C and blood pressure values, so we can keep the baseline A1C and BP consistent in the monthly table.

turns.inner_thought: I also want the DSME number to finally show the work the certified nurses completed. Several patients in the outlying clinics wrapped their telehealth series or individual diabetes education sessions, and clinically that's completed DSME. If the report only recognizes the formal class pathway, we'll understate the education our team delivered.
turns.utterance: Good. Also, the patients who have completed DSME should look better this month, because several telehealth classes and individual diabetes sessions wrapped up across the outlying clinics.

turns.inner_thought: Great, if those DSME completions are documented in the education module, the standard extract will pick them up. I don't want to start counting education based on narrative interpretation or local tracking sheets, because then the figure won't be reproducible. No need to overcomplicate it if the EHR completion flags are there.
turns.utterance: That's great progress. Once those DSME completions are reflected in the education module, I can roll that number into the report without changing the standard extract.

turns.inner_thought: I made sure the patient summaries note two recent outside-hospital admissions that came up during follow-up calls. We don't have the records back yet, but the nurses are already managing medication reconciliation and follow-up around those stays, so the last six months of hospital admissions should include them. Steering needs to see the real burden our team is handling.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I also added two recent outside-hospital admissions that came up on follow-up calls, so the last six months of hospital admissions are fully represented in the patient summaries.

turns.inner_thought: I'll finalize the deck from the admission feed and confirmed encounter data, same as always. If those outside stays aren't in the ADT or coded encounter tables yet, they won't be in my utilization counts, but her note probably just means the summaries are current on her side. As long as I keep the steering tables tied to the current feed, the methodology stays clean.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I'll finalize the steering deck using the current admission feed and circulate the completed packet once the monthly tables are refreshed.
